record.title: A paper proposes carbon reporting and a smallest-model selection rule for AI research
record.summary: The authors introduce carbonbenchmark, which combines CodeCarbon measurements with fitted training curves, and propose a “Smallest Model that Achieves the Job” (SMAJ) selection approach. They report illustrative fits on Fashion-MNIST, GLUE SST-2 and UCI Adult, and an automated review of 5,285 NeurIPS 2025 papers using LLM classification. Their proprietary-inference emissions examples use assumed active parameter counts and generic hardware/grid factors; these are estimates, not measured model-specific emissions. The paper argues for reporting research emissions and treating environmental cost alongside accuracy.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The authors provide carbonbenchmark, combining CodeCarbon measurements with fitted training curves, and demonstrate it on three small tasks using an RTX 4060 Ti over a one-hour training period.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The authors propose SMAJ as a cost-aware model-selection concept and recommend reporting research emissions; the paper does not establish a generally validated equivalence or noninferiority procedure for selecting the smallest adequate model.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The reported review of 5,285 NeurIPS 2025 papers classifies papers with LLMs after a 200-paper model-agreement study; its corpus estimates are automated classifications, not a human-adjudicated census.

evidence_gaps.description: No independent validation on frontier-scale training or inference workloads.

brief.importance_rationale: If its measurement proposals prove reliable at larger scales, they could make energy and carbon costs visible in AI research and model selection. Current experiments are small and several inference inputs are assumptions, so this is a methods proposal rather than a validated standard.
limitations: Training examples cover only three small tasks and one local GPU; they do not establish frontier-scale measurement accuracy.
The NeurIPS paper-use estimates rely on automated classification rather than human adjudication.
Proprietary inference emissions use assumed active parameter counts and generic hardware/grid factors, not measured per-model energy.
SMAJ’s uncertainty threshold is not a demonstrated equivalence design and may require selection-bias control.

They report illustrative fits on Fashion-MNIST, GLUE SST-2 and UCI Adult, and an automated review of 5,285 NeurIPS 2025 papers using LLM classification. technical.claimed_result: Authors recommend reporting study emissions and propose training-curve and smallest-adequate-model metrics.
technical.demonstrated_result: The primary paper describes its tool, methods and illustrative experiments; the research desk did not independently run the code or validate emissions estimates.
technical.mechanism: Measures local training emissions and fits exponential, delayed-exponential and power-law learning curves; proposes a single-parameter training-efficiency measure and SMAJ selection framing.
technical.regime: Illustrations on Fashion-MNIST, GLUE SST-2 and UCI Adult, local RTX 4060 Ti training, plus an automated review of 5,285 NeurIPS 2025 papers.
technical.strongest_baseline: The paper discusses accuracy-focused state-of-the-art selection and common learning-curve forms; no validated environmental benchmark baseline is established.

brief.title: A paper proposes carbon reporting and a smallest-model selection rule for AI research
brief.why_it_matters: Environmental measurement choices can affect comparisons of model quality and compute cost. This paper offers methods and a reporting proposal, but its small training examples and assumed frontier-inference inputs do not establish reliable footprint estimates or a validated model-selection standard.
